purpose: Adversarial privacy-safe regression for rhetorical-ladder judgment coverage, self-cancelling assertions, induced follow-ups, counterfactual turn deletion, portability, and preservation of valid banter/public-background/social-anecdote distinctions.

cases.name: UNSUPPORTED_ALONE_RETORT_SELF_CANCELS
cases.scene: A friendly child asks whether B is alone. B says a confident line implying B is not alone. The child asks who else is coming. B immediately admits B does not know. No enemy, bluff, concealment, face-saving, relationship grievance or task effect supports the false implication.

cases.name: STRATEGIC_ALONE_BLUFF
cases.scene: An armed pursuer asks whether B is alone. B falsely implies allies are nearby while deliberately looking toward a dark doorway. The pursuer slows and checks the doorway, allowing B to escape.

cases.name: GENERIC_Q_RETORT_Q_PUNCHLINE_DELETION
cases.scene: A four-turn Q-retort-follow-up-punchline exchange can be reduced to the final truthful answer with no loss of task information, relationship pressure, concealment or decision. Only generic joke cadence is lost.

cases.name: SHARED_HISTORY_YEAR_CORRECTION
cases.scene: Friends argue whether they last met two, three or four years ago. A final correction reveals one friend was excluded from a later gathering, creating a specific relationship grievance and prompting a compensation promise.

cases.name: CONFLICTING_TASK_GOALS_ABSURD_NEGOTIATION
cases.scene: One group wants a prisoner alive for a reward while another wants the same prisoner drowned for revenge. Their seemingly comic exchange is an actual negotiation over physical control of the prisoner.
cases.focus: absurd humor generated by concrete conflict

cases.name: PORTABLE_GENERIC_TEASE
cases.scene: A teasing retort and punchline contain no shared-history reference, no current object/task dependence and no downstream relationship action; the same exchange could be moved to unrelated characters unchanged.

cases.name: FACE_SAVING_DEFLECTION_WITH_EVIDENCE
cases.scene: A junior asks a superior whether the superior is afraid. The superior jokes instead of answering while subordinates are watching, then privately changes the plan once they leave. Status pressure and later behavior support face-saving deflection.

cases.name: REVIEWER_INVENTS_FACE_SAVING
cases.scene: A retort could theoretically be face-saving, but no audience, status pressure, embarrassment, later behavior or relationship context supports that interpretation.

cases.name: PUBLIC_BACKGROUND_BUNDLE_STILL_FAILS
cases.scene: A local child tells an experienced participant the current event, the participant's own role, reward amount, rumor spread and outsider count. Only the outsider count is new and actionable.

cases.name: FIRSTHAND_PERSONAL_ANECDOTE_STILL_PASSES
cases.scene: After being asked whether the speaker saw a mutual acquaintance, the speaker recounts a short firsthand funny incident about that acquaintance. The relationship supports casual storytelling and the anecdote does not restate the listener's mission or public setup.

cases.name: TEMPORAL_SPENDING_SCOPE_STILL_FAILS
cases.scene: Money is obtained last night, a spending list is given with no scope break, and one listed person's consumption is then explicitly dated two days earlier.

cases.name: RISK_QUESTION_PARTIAL_ANSWER
cases.scene: A child asks whether an adult will be alone in danger. The adult avoids naming uncertain help and instead gives a direct instruction that changes the child's safety behavior. The avoidance serves protection rather than punchline setup.

cases.name: TEMPORARY_FALSE_STATE_NOT_DELTA
cases.scene: A retort briefly makes the listener believe help exists, but the next line immediately reveals the speaker has no knowledge of any help. The temporary belief causes no action, risk, relationship or strategic effect except prompting the next question.
cases.focus: temporary false state is not meaningful delta

cases.name: MATERIAL_MISDIRECTION_DELTA
cases.scene: A false retort causes the listener to choose the wrong corridor, giving the speaker time to hide evidence. The lie is immediately actionable misdirection.

cases.name: Rhetorical_Ladder_Record_Parity_Missing
cases.scene: The candidate inventory lists five rhetorical ladders, but the audit emits explicit anti-template records for only four before claiming no template failures.

cases.name: Rhetorical_Ladder_Record_Parity_Complete
cases.scene: Every harvested rhetorical ladder receives a dedicated turn-by-turn anti-template record, including PASS cases with located relationship/task evidence.
